title: Ignaz Semmelweis's birth chart
metaDescription: Ignaz Semmelweis's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 8.9° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Neptune sit 0.7° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads drive and imagination as a single working part. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 8.9° Cancer. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by the Moon in the classical scheme — a water sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 21.9° Gemini; Venus stands at 7.4° Leo; Mars stands at 24.0° Leo. The tradition reads a mind at home in argument and pattern from Mercury, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate from Venus, drive that ignites on contact from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Neptune — a trine holding at 0.7°. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Saturn square Uranus at 0.9°, and the Sun opposition Jupiter at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Uranus while both square Saturn. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. Venus stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mercury in Gemini at 21.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 8.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 fire, 3 water, 2 air, 1 earth; by modality, 6 mutable, 2 cardinal, 2 fixed. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.8° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 15.4°.
